meetings.async-video.question: I want to kill the status meeting. What should I use to record a screen video and share it?

method.how: Ranked on the half of the job people forget: sharing. A recorder is easy; a link that plays for someone outside your company, with a transcript, without an install or a sign-in wall, is the hard part. Free tiers were judged on whether they survive real use rather than a demo — a 5-minute cap, a 25-video lifetime allowance or a rolling delete of old captures all count against a tool. Then price per seat, then whether transcripts, captions, password links and access restrictions come with the advertised price or one tier above it. One open, self-hostable option and one genuinely free option are included on purpose.
method.tested_on: Not independently tested. No recordings were made, no viewer experience was timed, no upload speeds measured. Prices, tier limits and feature gates were read from each vendor's own pricing or repository page on 2026-08-29 and are quoted as written there. Where a vendor does not publish a number, this entry says so instead of guessing.
method.conflicts: None. No affiliate links, no paid placements, no relationship with any tool listed.
method.blind_note: No independent benchmark exists for async screen recorders — nobody runs a neutral lab on share-link latency, playback reliability or transcript accuracy. Search results for this category are almost entirely vendor comparison pages (every tool ranks itself first) and affiliate listicles paid per signup. Treat any ranking here, including this one, as an argument rather than a measurement.

ranked.name: Loom
ranked.one_liner: The default. Recipients just watch. Everything else fights this.
ranked.use_it_when: You send updates to people outside your team and cannot ask them to install anything, sign into anything, or download a file.
ranked.cost: Free tier (25 videos, 5-minute cap). Paid $18-$24/user/mo.
ranked.pricing_detail: Starter (free): 25 videos per person, 5-minute screen recordings, transcription in 50+ languages, video privacy controls, workspace up to 50 members. Business $18/user/mo: unlimited videos and unlimited recording time, up to 4K, transcripts plus closed captions, password protection, default privacy settings, basic waveform editing; vendor states annual billing saves 17%. Business + Loom AI $24/user/mo: adds auto-summaries, filler-word removal, edit-by-transcript, auto video enhancement. Enterprise: custom, adds SSO, SCIM and a stated 99.95% uptime SLA (vendor's figure). All read from loom.com/pricing on 2026-08-29.
ranked.good_at: The viewer end. A link opens and plays in a browser with no account, no app and no download, which is the single thing that decides whether async video actually replaces the meeting. Transcription in 50+ languages is on the free tier, not held back as an upsell, and comments land against a timestamp so replies are about a moment rather than the whole video.
ranked.the_catch: The free 5-minute screen cap is roughly one minute short of a real update, and the 25 videos are per person, not per month — you hit that wall once and stay behind it forever. The features that rescue a rambling first take, filler-word removal and edit-by-transcript, are on the $24 tier and not the $18 one, so the advertised price is not the price you end up on. It is per seat: five people recording is $90-$120 a month whether they record daily or twice a quarter.
ranked.wrong_for: Anyone whose recordings cannot sit on a US vendor's cloud, or who wants a one-off cost instead of a seat licence — self-host Cap. Anyone whose real problem is cutting the video rather than sending it — Descript.

ranked.name: Cap
ranked.one_liner: Open source, self-hostable, and the cheapest hosted sharing here.
ranked.use_it_when: Recordings cannot live on someone else's infrastructure, or you want Loom's shape at roughly a third of the seat price and are willing to read a licence.
ranked.cost: Free (personal use, 5-minute links). $29/yr desktop. Pro from $8.16/user/mo.
ranked.pricing_detail: Free: Studio Mode with full editor, 4K/60fps export, team workspaces — but shareable links are capped at 5 minutes and the pricing page states personal use only. Desktop Licence $29/year billed yearly, described as a perpetual licence: unlimited local recording and editing, commercial usage rights, 20 cloud share links a month at up to 5 minutes each. Cap Pro $12/user/mo billed monthly or $8.16/user/mo billed annually (vendor states 32% off): unlimited cloud storage and bandwidth, AI titles, summaries, chapters and transcription, custom domain, password-protected shares, viewer analytics, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and HIPAA compliance claims. Enterprise: custom, adds managed self-hosting, SAML SSO, SCIM. Code is AGPLv3, with the cap-camera* and scap-* crate families under MIT; the repo documents self-hosting via docker compose, plus Railway and Coolify deployment. Read from cap.so/pricing and github.com/CapSoftware/Cap on 2026-08-29.
ranked.good_at: Being the only credible pick here you can run yourself. The repo ships docker compose self-hosting, so the recordings and the share links stay on your infrastructure — and the AGPLv3 licence means that right is not revocable. On the hosted side, $8.16/user/mo annual with transcription, password shares and a custom domain undercuts every other hosted option in this entry.
ranked.the_catch: Two separate 5-minute walls plus a licence line most buyers skim: the free desktop tier is sold as personal use only, so recording work updates on it means the $29/year licence as a floor, and that licence still limits you to 20 cloud links a month at 5 minutes each. Transcripts, password-protected shares and unlimited link length are Pro-only. Self-hosting is genuine but not free of work — you own the object storage bill, the domain, the upgrades and any outage, and the managed version of it is an Enterprise line item with no published price.
ranked.wrong_for: Anyone who wants zero administration and a comment, reaction and analytics layer that has had years of polish — Loom. Anyone who wants unlimited recording at zero cost and can live without hosting — Screenity.

ranked.name: Vidyard
ranked.one_liner: The only free tier that lets a video run 30 minutes.
ranked.use_it_when: You send a handful of genuinely long updates each month — a walkthrough, a design review — and refuse to buy a seat licence for something that fires five times.
ranked.cost: Free: 5 videos/month, 30 min each. Paid tiers: price not published.
ranked.pricing_detail: Free $0: 5 videos per month, up to 30 minutes per video, 15 AI avatar videos with stock and 3 custom avatars, basic sharing. Captions are not included on free and password protection is not included on free. Starter: no price shown on the pricing page, 14-day trial, unlimited recordings and unlimited length, password-protected videos, branded sharing page, folder management; automated captions listed as an add-on. Teams: custom pricing, described as best for 5+ users, includes custom captions, customisable CTAs and CRM/MAP integrations. Enterprise: custom pricing, adds SSO, custom permissions, IP access control and domain playback restrictions. Check current pricing — on 2026-08-29 no per-seat number was published for Starter, Teams or Enterprise.
ranked.good_at: Length on a free plan. Thirty minutes is enough for a proper walkthrough, where the 5-minute caps at Loom, Cap and Zight force you to split or upgrade. The monthly allowance also resets, unlike Loom's lifetime 25, so an occasional recorder never accumulates a wall. At the top end the access controls are the strictest here — IP access control and domain playback restrictions, if you can afford Enterprise.
ranked.the_catch: You cannot budget for it. Only the free tier has a published number; everything above it is a sales conversation, which is a slow, quote-shaped way to buy a screen recorder. Captions are absent from free entirely and listed as an add-on on Starter, so the long video you recorded ships without a transcript unless you pay for it separately. The whole product is aimed at selling to prospects — CTAs, viewer tracking, CRM hooks — which is overhead you carry for what is meant to be a note to colleagues.
ranked.wrong_for: Anyone who needs a price before committing, or who wants a transcript by default — Loom includes transcription on free, Cap Pro bundles it.

ranked.name: Zight
ranked.one_liner: One tool and one link format for clips, screenshots and GIFs.
ranked.use_it_when: Your update is usually two screenshots, a GIF and a short clip, and you are tired of three tools producing three kinds of link.
ranked.cost: Free (5 min, 720p, last 50 captures). Paid $12.95-$15/user/mo.
ranked.pricing_detail: Share (free, 1 user): 5-minute maximum recordings, up to 720p, 1 GB storage, 5 video requests a month, 15-second GIFs, capture history limited to the last 50 captures. Create $12.95/user/mo, 2 users: unlimited recording time and uploads, automatic transcription in 50+ languages, AI captions and summaries, redaction and annotation. Collaborate $15/user/mo, up to 100 users: adds advanced analytics with viewer emails and watch percentages, custom branding and custom domain, restricted viewing access, password protection, GDPR and SOC 2 Type II. Scale: custom, adds HIPAA with BAA, SSO/SCIM, custom data retention and S3 storage. Vendor lists 20% off annual billing. Read from zight.com/pricing on 2026-08-29.
ranked.good_at: Mixed-media updates. Screenshots, annotated stills, 15-second GIFs and video all come out of one capture tool with one share-link pattern, so a written update with three inline visuals stops being a scavenger hunt across tools. Redaction is on the entry paid tier rather than reserved for enterprise, which matters if your screen has customer data on it.
ranked.the_catch: The free plan keeps only your last 50 captures, and screenshots count towards that number — a normal week of clipping silently pushes last month's video off the end, and there is no upgrade path that brings it back. Free is also 720p, which makes IDE and spreadsheet text unreadable, so the free tier is a demo rather than a plan. Transcription starts at Create, and everything most people mean by privacy — password, restricted viewing, custom domain — is Collaborate at $15/user/mo. Create is sold as a 2-user plan, so hiring a third person moves the whole team to the higher tier.
ranked.wrong_for: Pure video updates going to people outside your company — Loom does that better for similar money. Long recordings on a free plan — Vidyard.

ranked.name: Screenity
ranked.one_liner: Genuinely free and unlimited. You solve the sharing yourself.
ranked.use_it_when: Budget is zero, the recording must never touch a vendor's cloud, and you already have somewhere to put a file that your audience can open.
ranked.cost: Free. GPL-3.0 licensed. No paid tier.
ranked.pricing_detail: Free, no accounts, no tiers. Licensed GPL-3.0 from version 3.0.0 onwards, so commercial use is permitted under the licence terms. The project states no limits on recording length or number of recordings. Optional Google Drive integration produces share links; a self-hosted build is stated to make no API calls and operate entirely offline. Latest release read as 4.4.12, dated 2 June 2026, from 66 releases. Read from github.com/alyssaxuu/screenity on 2026-08-29.
ranked.good_at: Removing every limit the paid tools sell you out of. No cap on length, no monthly allowance, no account, no upload, no retention clock, and annotation tools while you record. If your compliance position is that video of your screen must not leave the machine, this is the shortest path to that being literally true.
ranked.the_catch: It records; it does not share, and sharing is half this job. There is no hosted player, so your link is a Google Drive file — which drops your viewer straight into Drive's permission model, the sign-in wall you were trying to escape, with no transcript, no captions, no comments and no view counts. It is Chrome-only, and it is essentially one maintainer, so when a Chrome extension platform change breaks recording you wait rather than escalate.
ranked.wrong_for: Anyone sending updates to clients or anyone outside your Google domain — Loom or Cap. Anyone who needs transcripts or captions, which is anyone with a deaf colleague or a non-native-speaker team — every other tool here.

also_considered.name: Screen Studio
also_considered.why_not: Best-looking output of anything here, but macOS only and it is now a subscription: screen.studio shows $9/month billed monthly and $108/year billed annually, with older one-time licences honoured. It is a polish tool — you edit every video — which is the opposite of a daily async update.

also_considered.name: Descript
also_considered.why_not: Free is capped at 60 minutes of media a month, 720p and watermarked exports, 5 GB storage and one seat; real use starts at Hobbyist $16/user/mo. It is an editing suite that can share, not a record-and-send tool.

also_considered.name: Claap
also_considered.why_not: The free plan is 10 videos per user, 300 minutes total and 3 months of storage — old videos are deleted, not archived. Pro and Business prices are not shown on the pricing page.

also_considered.name: Guidde
also_considered.why_not: Free covers up to 25 how-to videos with link sharing, but it builds step-by-step documentation rather than a talking update; watermark removal is Pro at $19/mo annual or $29/mo monthly.

also_considered.name: Tella
also_considered.why_not: Pro $13/mo, Premium $19/mo, and the pricing page does not state what the free plan actually allows. Aimed at polished published video — removing Tella branding needs the $19 tier.

also_considered.name: mmhmm
also_considered.why_not: Effectively discontinued as a product line: mmhmm.app now redirects to airtime.com, run by the same company (footer reads mmhmm inc., 2020-2026). Do not build a team habit on it.

watch_list: Loom under Atlassian: whether the free Starter tier keeps its 25 videos and 5-minute recordings at all, and whether AI editing drops from the $24 tier into the $18 one.
Cap clarifying its free-tier wording — personal use only sits awkwardly beside an AGPLv3 codebase, and a clean answer would make Cap much easier to recommend to businesses.
Vidyard publishing a Starter price. Hidden per-seat pricing is the main reason it sits third rather than higher.
Any vendor abandoning per-seat pricing. Async video is broadcast — charging per recorder while viewers are free is the only sane model, and per-seat maths still punishes wide rollouts.
Screen Studio shipping Windows, which would move it from a macOS niche into the main list.
Retention clauses generally: Zight's last-50-captures and Claap's 3-month storage are exactly the kind of limit that tightens without an announcement, and old updates vanish.

meetings.chat-with-pdfs.question: I have 200 PDFs and a deadline. What answers questions across all of them without quietly citing the wrong file?

method.how: Ranked on one thing: how hard the tool makes it to accept a confident answer pulled from the wrong document. Top marks for a click-through citation that lands you on the quoted text, and for the ability to tick sources on and off so you control what got searched. Price and document limits broke ties, because most people hit a page or source cap long before they hit a quality ceiling. Tools that reason beautifully but cannot show you where the sentence came from were demoted regardless of how good the prose reads.
method.tested_on: Not independently tested. No PDFs were run through any of these. Every price, limit and citation claim was read from the vendor's own page or repository on 2026-08-29 and is quoted or marked unreadable.
method.conflicts: None. No affiliate links, no paid placements, no relationship with any tool listed.
method.blind_note: There is no independent benchmark for consumer document-QA products. Academic RAG benchmarks test retrieval components, not these apps, and none of the vendors here publish a hallucination or attribution-accuracy number you can check. Search results for this category are dominated by vendors ranking themselves and by affiliate listicles, so treat any 'best PDF chat' page, including this one, as a starting point rather than evidence.

ranked.name: Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM)
ranked.one_liner: Free, tightly grounded, and it shows you the quote
ranked.use_it_when: You have up to 50 mixed documents, you want to check every claim, and you would rather not pay anything to find out whether this approach works at all.
ranked.cost: Free tier. Paid via Google AI plans $4.99-$199.99/mo.
ranked.pricing_detail: Free: 50 sources per notebook, 100 notebooks, 50 chat queries/day. Google AI Plus $4.99/mo: 100 sources, 200 notebooks, 200 queries/day. Google AI Pro $19.99/mo: 300 sources, 500 notebooks, 500 queries/day. Google AI Ultra from $99.99/mo: 500 sources, 2.5K queries/day, or $199.99/mo: 600 sources, 5K queries/day. Each source can hold up to 500,000 words or 200MB. Note: the per-notebook numbers come from Google's own limits article, but the renamed Gemini Notebook help page now states only 'two times', 'four times' and '5x or 20x' higher than standard, without the figures.
ranked.good_at: Citations. Answers carry clickable inline citations; hovering shows the full quoted text and clicking navigates to that quote in the source. Checkboxes on each source let you exclude documents from a question, so you can force an answer to come from the three files you actually care about.
ranked.the_catch: It cites the passage, not the page. Google's docs describe navigation to the quote and hover-to-see-quote, with no mention of a page number, so pasting a reference into a memo means finding the page yourself. Fifty chat queries a day on free goes fast on a real pile, and the source checkboxes cut both ways: an untick you forgot about silently removes a document from the answer with no warning.
ranked.wrong_for: Anyone who needs 'contract.pdf, p.41' printed in the answer, or whose documents cannot go to Google. Use Acrobat AI Assistant for the first, RAGFlow self-hosted for the second.

ranked.name: Acrobat AI Assistant
ranked.one_liner: Citations that land inside the PDF you already own
ranked.use_it_when: PDFs are your working format, you already pay Adobe, and you want the answer and the source page in the same window rather than two tabs.
ranked.cost: $1.99/mo add-on to Acrobat Pro. Acrobat Studio $24.99/mo annual.
ranked.pricing_detail: AI Assistant add-on $1.99/mo for existing Acrobat Pro subscribers (Acrobat Pro itself is $19.99/mo, $239.88/yr prepaid). Acrobat Studio, which bundles AI Assistant, is $24.99/mo on the annual plan billed monthly, $34.99/mo month-to-month, or $299.88/yr prepaid. Business team licences from $23.99 per licence per month. A PDF Space can combine up to 100 files and links.
ranked.good_at: Working where the documents already live. Adobe states answers are 'always cited back to your source documents' with 'precise citations that link directly to the source in your docs', and it says your content is never used to train Adobe's models. PDF Spaces holding 100 files makes it viable for a real deal room rather than a demo folder.
ranked.the_catch: The $1.99 headline is an add-on price, not a price. It only applies on top of an Acrobat Pro subscription, so the real monthly cost is about $22 or you jump to Studio at $24.99 on an annual commitment shown as a monthly figure. Adobe's own AI Assistant pages do not publish per-file page or size limits, so the ceiling on a large scanned document is unknown until you hit it.
ranked.wrong_for: Anyone not already in the Adobe estate, and anyone with mostly Word, web pages or transcripts rather than PDFs. Gemini Notebook handles mixed sources and costs nothing.

ranked.name: RAGFlow
ranked.one_liner: Apache-2.0, self-hostable, and you can inspect the chunks
ranked.use_it_when: The documents cannot leave your infrastructure, or you need to see and fix how they were split before you trust an answer.
ranked.cost: Self-host free (Apache-2.0). Cloud: free, $29/mo, $129/mo.
ranked.pricing_detail: Self-hosting is free under Apache-2.0, which permits commercial and multi-tenant use. Minimum spec from the repo: CPU >= 4 cores, RAM >= 16 GB, disk >= 50 GB, Docker >= 24.0.0 with Compose >= v2.26.1. Hosted: Free $0/mo with 0.1 GB storage and 500 credits, Starter $29/mo with 5 GB and 5,000 credits, Pro $129/mo with 50 GB and 20,000 credits, Enterprise custom with on-premises and BYOC deployment.
ranked.good_at: Auditability of the retrieval itself, which is where wrong-document answers are actually born. It advertises 'grounded citations with reduced hallucinations', 'traceable citations' and 'visualization of text chunking to allow human intervention', so you can see the chunks a document was split into and correct bad ones instead of guessing why the model quoted the wrong appendix.
ranked.the_catch: It is infrastructure, not an app. Sixteen gigabytes of RAM and a Docker Compose stack is a Tuesday afternoon before you have asked one question, and the answer quality is now your problem: your embedding model, your chunk sizes, your parser. The hosted free tier's 0.1 GB of storage is a taster, not a trial of anything real.
ranked.wrong_for: Anyone who wants to upload a folder and ask a question this morning. Take Gemini Notebook or ChatDOC and come back to RAGFlow when compliance says no.

ranked.name: ChatDOC
ranked.one_liner: Footnotes that highlight the exact text on the page
ranked.use_it_when: You are checking specific claims in long documents and want the citation to open the page with the sentence highlighted, not a paraphrase.
ranked.cost: Free tier (3 pages per file). Paid plan: check current pricing.
ranked.pricing_detail: Free: 10 file uploads per day, 100 questions per day, but only 3 pages per file and PDF only. Pro: unlimited uploads, unlimited daily questions, unlimited pages per file, and support for PDF, DOC, DOCX, scans, websites, EPUB, MD and TXT. Prices did not render on the pricing page when read on 2026-08-29 (currency placeholders only) and the file size limits displayed as 'NaN MB', so treat the paid figure as unverified until you see it in the checkout.
ranked.good_at: Making verification a click. Its citation feature is built around footnotes that reveal context, highlighted text and quote views inside the document, which is the fastest way to catch an answer that came from the wrong file. The free tier's 100 questions a day is unusually generous for interrogating a document hard.
ranked.the_catch: The free tier reads three pages per file. That is a demo dressed as a plan, and it will happily answer questions about a 90-page report on the strength of its cover and contents page, which is exactly the failure you are trying to avoid. Add that the vendor does not render its own prices, and you are committing without knowing the number.
ranked.wrong_for: Anyone who needs a price before they commit, or who needs more than PDFs on the free plan. Humata publishes its numbers; Gemini Notebook takes any file type for nothing.

ranked.name: Humata
ranked.one_liner: Cheap entry, but pages are the currency here
ranked.use_it_when: You want a small paid tool with published prices and a handful of colleagues, and your total page count is genuinely modest.
ranked.cost: Free 60 pages. Expert $9.99/mo. Team $49/user/mo.
ranked.pricing_detail: Free: $0, 60 pages, 1 user, no page top-ups. Expert: $9.99/mo, 500 free pages, 3 users, then $0.02 per additional page. Team: $49 per user per month, 5,000 free pages, up to 10 users, then $0.01 per additional page. Enterprise: custom allowance and pricing, unlimited users. File size limits are not published.
ranked.good_at: Being legible. It is the only tool here that puts a clear per-page number on the table, which makes the cost of a big one-off job something you can estimate before you start rather than discover. Answers carry highlighted citations you can trace back.
ranked.the_catch: Pages are the meter, and PDFs are long. Two deposition transcripts or one board pack will eat the 500-page Expert allowance in an afternoon, after which every extra page is $0.02 whether the answer was useful or not. The free tier's 60 pages is barely one document. And the site describes 'citations' and 'highlights' without ever documenting page numbers, so the precision you are buying is unclear.
ranked.wrong_for: High-volume work, and anyone with scanned or image-heavy files where page counts balloon. Self-host RAGFlow, or use Gemini Notebook where the limit is sources rather than pages.

also_considered.name: ChatPDF
also_considered.why_not: Free plan is 2 documents a day, and the site would not render its paid prices or limits on any page read on 2026-08-29.

also_considered.name: Claude Projects / ChatGPT Projects
also_considered.why_not: Best reasoning across a messy pile, but answers are not anchored to a clickable page, which is precisely the failure mode here; neither vendor publishes per-project file limits.

also_considered.name: Open WebUI
also_considered.why_not: Free to self-host, but the Open WebUI License adds a requirement to preserve the 'Open WebUI' branding unless you buy the enterprise plan, which rules out white-labelled internal deployments.

also_considered.name: Onyx Community Edition
also_considered.why_not: MIT and genuinely self-hostable, but it is built to search your connected company apps rather than a folder of loose PDFs, and the useful org features sit in a separate Enterprise Edition.

also_considered.name: AnythingLLM
also_considered.why_not: MIT, free desktop app with source citations, but you supply the model and tune the retrieval yourself, so it is RAGFlow's problem with less of RAGFlow's tooling.

also_considered.name: Elicit
also_considered.why_not: Excellent at academic papers, priced at $49/mo Pro and $169/mo Scale, and no help at all with contracts, board packs or invoices.

watch_list: Google has renamed NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook and its current help page states limits only as 'two times' or 'four times' standard rather than the 50/100/300/500 source figures still published in the older limits article. If the hard numbers stay hidden, the free tier stops being something you can plan around.
The first mainstream tool that prints a real locator in the answer text, 'contract.pdf, p.41', rather than a hover-to-see-quote, takes the top slot outright.
Whether Adobe folds AI Assistant into Acrobat Pro instead of charging $1.99 on top. That single change would make it the cheapest credible pick for PDF-native work.
ChatDOC publishing prices on its own pricing page. Until then it cannot be recommended above a tool whose number you can read.
RAGFlow staying Apache-2.0 across the whole product. Open-core drift, where citation or parsing quality moves into an enterprise-only edition, would change the self-host recommendation.
OCR quality on scanned documents. Every tool here is strong on born-digital PDFs and none publishes an accuracy figure for scans, which is where wrong-document answers cluster.

ops.bookkeeping.question: Which bookkeeping tool should I run my books on, and does it actually handle my country's tax — GST included?

method.how: Country coverage decided the order more than features. A ledger that cannot file your VAT, GST or sales tax is a spreadsheet with better fonts, so each pick was checked against the vendor's own regional editions — including whether an India site exists at all. After that: bank-feed coverage (does it pull transactions automatically, and is that gated behind a higher tier), what the second legal entity costs, and whether a human bookkeeper is bundled or a separate quote-only contract. Nothing here is bad software; the failure mode in this category is buying the wrong regional edition, not buying a bad product.
method.tested_on: Not independently tested. No books were kept, no bank feed was connected, no return was filed. Every price and limit was read from the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-08-29 and is quoted as found — list price, not the promotional first-six-months figure. Regional availability was checked by fetching the vendor's own country URL.
method.conflicts: None. No affiliate links, no paid placements, no relationship with any tool listed.
method.blind_note: There is no independent benchmark for bookkeeping software. Nobody runs a standardised set of 5,000 transactions through Xero, QuickBooks and Zoho Books and publishes the categorisation accuracy. Be warned that search results for 'best accounting software' are almost entirely affiliate-commission review sites and vendors ranking themselves — accounting software pays some of the highest referral fees in SaaS, and the ranking usually reflects that. Treat any list that does not show you a vendor pricing page as advertising.

ranked.name: Xero
ranked.one_liner: Best bank reconciliation in the business — if your country is covered.
ranked.use_it_when: You are a UK, US, Australian, New Zealand or Canadian business and reconciling the bank account is the job you hate most. Also the right answer if you have several entities and want them all in one login with one accountant.
ranked.cost: UK £18-£70/mo. US $25-$90/mo. CA $25-$80/mo. Per entity.
ranked.pricing_detail: UK list: Ignite £18, Grow £39, Comprehensive £55, Ultimate £70 per month, all excluding VAT, with 90% off for the first six months. US list: Early $25, Growing $55, Established $90. Canada: Starter C$25, Standard C$60, Premium C$80. Priced per organisation, so a second company is a second full subscription — no group discount on the pricing page. Add-ons stack fast on UK Ignite: auto-reconcile is £3.50/mo extra, CIS returns £5/mo, Company Accounts & Tax £120/yr, payroll £1.50 per person, Expenses and Projects £2.50 per extra user. US payroll is Gusto-powered at $36/mo plus $6 per employee. Direct bank feeds are free for most customers, but Xero states some UK banks charge a fee that is passed on to you, and the US page refers to chargeable direct bank feeds invoiced separately. No in-house bookkeeping service — a human is a separate contract with a Xero advisor.
ranked.good_at: Bank feeds and the reconcile screen. Xero's whole design centres on clearing the bank line by line, and the suggested-match behaviour plus bank rules is why bookkeepers move clients onto it. Multi-entity practice tooling and the advisor network are genuinely deep in the UK, Australia and New Zealand.
ranked.the_catch: The US Early plan at $25 caps you at 20 invoices and 5 bills a month, and does not include auto-reconcile — that is manual matching only. Cross either limit and you are on Growing at $55, a 120% jump. Multi-currency, project tracking and employee expense claims are gated all the way up to Established at $90. And the headline price you signed up on is 90% off for six months; month seven is a four-to-ten-fold increase on the same plan.
ranked.wrong_for: Indian businesses. xero.com/in/ returns a 404 — there is no India edition and no GSTR filing. Use Zoho Books. Also wrong if you want a bookkeeper bundled in: Xero sells software, not labour.

ranked.name: QuickBooks Online
ranked.one_liner: Biggest accountant network, deepest US tax hooks, highest list prices.
ranked.use_it_when: You are a US business, or a UK sole trader facing Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, and you want a bookkeeper you can hire on demand rather than going to find one. Also when your existing accountant has already said which one they want.
ranked.cost: US $38-$340/mo. UK list price not published without selecting a plan.
ranked.pricing_detail: US list: Simple Start $38 (1 user), Essentials $85 (3 users), Plus $140 (5 users), Advanced $340 (25 users), each with 2-3 free accountant seats. Current offer is 90% off for three months. The UK pricing page shows the plan ladder — Sole Trader Plus, Simple Start, Essentials, Plus, Advanced, with MTD for VAT and MTD for Income Tax flagged — but does not display the monthly figures until you pick a plan, so check current UK pricing at source before committing. Human help is a real product line: Expert Assisted (coaching), Expert Full Service Bookkeeping (a dedicated bookkeeper who categorises and reconciles monthly) and Expert Cleanup. None of them publish a price; the page routes you to a sales call. Assume it is extra, and assume a quote.
ranked.good_at: Availability of humans. If you want to stop doing this yourself, Intuit will sell you a bookkeeper inside the same product, which no other tool on this list does natively. The US accountant and tax-preparer network is the largest, and the sales-tax and 1099 plumbing is the most mature.
ranked.the_catch: US list prices are the highest in this category by a wide margin — $140/mo for Plus is roughly 2.5x Xero Growing for comparable ground — and the 90% discount lasts only three months before the full rate lands. The bookkeeping add-on that makes it worth choosing is quote-only, so you cannot budget for the thing you are buying it for.
ranked.wrong_for: India, absolutely and permanently. Intuit ended new sign-ups in July 2022, cut off existing subscribers on 30 April 2023, and states that as of 1 July 2023 there is no access to QuickBooks products in India at all. Indian readers should go straight to Zoho Books or TallyPrime. Cost-sensitive UK sole traders should look at FreeAgent instead.

ranked.name: Zoho Books
ranked.one_liner: Only serious option with native India GST and a real free tier.
ranked.use_it_when: You are in India and need GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, e-invoicing and e-way bills out of the same ledger you keep the books in. Or you are anywhere and want to spend a tenth of what QuickBooks costs.
ranked.cost: Free under ₹25 lakh / $50k revenue. India ₹899-₹9,599/mo. US $20-$275/mo.
ranked.pricing_detail: India: Free (₹0, 1 user plus accountant, 1,000 invoices and 1,000 bills a year), Standard ₹899/mo, Professional ₹1,799, Premium ₹3,599, Elite ₹5,999, Ultimate ₹9,599; roughly 17% off paying annually (Standard drops to ₹749/mo). Extra users ₹180/mo. US: Free ($0), Standard $20, Professional $50, Premium $70, Elite $150, Ultimate $275; extra users $3/mo. The free plan is available indefinitely provided financial-year revenue stays under ₹25 lakh in India or $50k in the US. Editions exist for the US, UK, Australia, Canada, India, Germany, France, Mexico and the Gulf states (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Qatar), with Arabic UI in some. Billed per organisation, so entity two is a second subscription. No human bookkeeping service of any kind.
ranked.good_at: India. Nothing else on this list files a GSTR. It is also the only tool here where a genuinely free plan gives you a full double-entry ledger rather than a demo, and the price gap to QuickBooks is a factor of ten at the low end.
ranked.the_catch: GST reports and filing, e-invoicing and the audit trail are listed against the paid plans — the free tier is a ledger, not a compliance tool, so the moment you actually need to file you are on Standard. The revenue cap is on the financial year, not on what you have billed so far, so crossing it mid-year moves you onto a paid plan retrospectively in practice. And Zoho's gravity is strong: the useful bits (CRM, Inventory, Expense, Payroll) are separate subscriptions and the pitch quietly becomes Zoho One.
ranked.wrong_for: Anyone whose accountant only works in Xero or QuickBooks — the practice-side tooling and the pool of bookkeepers who know Zoho Books is much thinner outside India. Use whichever your accountant names.

ranked.name: FreeAgent
ranked.one_liner: Free forever with a NatWest or Mettle account. UK only.
ranked.use_it_when: You are a UK sole trader, limited company, LLP or landlord — especially one already banking with NatWest, RBS, Ulster Bank or Mettle, which makes the whole thing cost nothing.
ranked.cost: Free with NatWest/RBS/Ulster/Mettle. Otherwise £10-£33/mo + VAT.
ranked.pricing_detail: Priced by business type, not by feature tier: limited company £33/mo or £330/yr, partnership/LLP £27/mo or £270/yr, sole trader £19/mo or £190/yr, landlord £10/mo or £100/yr, all excluding 20% VAT, with 50% off the first six months. Free for the life of the account if you hold a NatWest, Royal Bank of Scotland or Ulster Bank business account, or a Mettle account with at least one transaction a month. Bank feeds and MTD-compatible VAT filing direct to HMRC are included on every plan, not gated. Add-ons: Smart Capture Unlimited £5/mo, Amazon integration £6/mo. Accountant access is included; an actual bookkeeper is your own separate hire.
ranked.good_at: Being free and complete at the same time. No other tool here gives a UK limited company bank feeds, VAT filing to HMRC and a full ledger at £0. For a one-person UK company it is the correct default answer and the others have to argue their way past it.
ranked.the_catch: The free tier is a bank marketing product, not a pricing plan. It lives as long as your NatWest, RBS, Ulster or Mettle account does — close or switch the account and you are on £33/mo for a limited company, which is above Xero Grow. Mettle also requires at least one transaction a month to keep it. You are letting your bank own your ledger, and the migration out is the usual accounting-data migration, which is to say unpleasant.
ranked.wrong_for: Anyone outside the UK — there is no US, Indian or EU edition. Anything with multiple entities, inventory or serious complexity: use Xero. Indian businesses: Zoho Books.

ranked.name: ERPNext (self-hosted)
ranked.one_liner: Self-hosted double-entry with India GST, if you have a sysadmin.
ranked.use_it_when: Your financial data cannot sit on someone else's server, or you are in India and want GST compliance without a per-seat subscription, and you have someone who can run a Linux box.
ranked.cost: Free self-hosted (AGPL-3.0). Frappe Cloud from $5/mo (₹410).
ranked.pricing_detail: The software is free and AGPL-3.0 licensed, with no user cap and no commercial-use restriction — you may run it in a business. Frappe Cloud, the vendor's managed hosting, starts at $5/mo (₹410) for a shared site, $20/mo (₹1,800) for a server hosting multiple sites, and $125/mo (₹5,400) for dedicated isolation. India GST comes from a separate free app, India Compliance (GPL-3.0), covering GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B preparation, GSTR-2A/2B purchase reconciliation for ITC, e-invoicing and e-way bill via the NIC portal, and live GSTIN validation. That app's automated government-API features require a paid India Compliance Account on top. There is no bundled human bookkeeper; implementation partners are a separate paid engagement. Frappe also ships Frappe Books, a free AGPL desktop app storing everything in a local SQLite file, if you want single-company offline bookkeeping with no server at all.
ranked.good_at: Ownership. Your ledger, your server, your backups, no per-seat tax and no vendor able to switch off your country the way Intuit switched off India. The India Compliance app is the strongest open-source GST implementation available.
ranked.the_catch: Automatic bank feeds are the weak point — the hosted competition connects to your bank in two clicks, and here you are largely importing statements or wiring up an integration yourself, which is precisely the daily labour you were trying to avoid. It is also an ERP: the accounting module assumes ERP concepts and a chart of accounts you configure, so the setup is days rather than an afternoon. AGPL-3.0 means if you modify it and offer it to others over a network, you owe them your source.
ranked.wrong_for: Solo founders and anyone without an operator on the team — the running cost is your time, and it will exceed £33/mo within a fortnight. Use FreeAgent in the UK, Zoho Books in India, Xero elsewhere.

also_considered.name: Bench
also_considered.why_not: Excluded: it collapsed. Bench shut off customer access without warning on 27 December 2024, filed for bankruptcy on 7 January 2025 with $65.4m of liabilities against $2.8m of cash, was bought by Employer.com and restarted in January 2025 — do not put your ledger somewhere that has already locked customers out once.

also_considered.name: Pilot
also_considered.why_not: US-only and the human is the expensive part: Essentials is $99/mo for AI categorisation with no human bookkeeper at all, and the Core plan that actually gives you a US-based bookkeeper is quote-only. Tax is a further $1,000-$2,450+/yr by entity type.

also_considered.name: Wave
also_considered.why_not: The free Starter plan explicitly excludes bank transaction auto-import, auto-categorisation and receipt scanning — the entire job. That is $19/mo Pro, and Wave is US and Canada only. Wave Advisors bookkeeping starts at $149/mo.

also_considered.name: TallyPrime
also_considered.why_not: Still the India default and it does file GSTR-1/3B, reconcile GSTR-2A/2B and generate e-invoices and e-way bills — but it is installed desktop software at ₹22,500 (Silver) to ₹67,500 (Gold) lifetime plus 18% GST, with TSS renewal from year two, and no real bank feed. Zoho Books is the cloud answer.

also_considered.name: Odoo Accounting
also_considered.why_not: The One App Free plan genuinely includes Accounting with hosting, and bank sync covers 28,000+ banks. Not ranked because the free tier is one app only — add anything else and you are on per-user pricing that the accounting page does not state, so you cannot see the real cost from the page that sells it to you.

watch_list: Whether Xero ships an India edition with GSTR filing. It would immediately outrank Zoho Books for Indian businesses that also trade abroad, and xero.com/in/ currently 404s.
Xero's 90%-off-for-six-months US promotion ends 30 September 2026. If list prices move rather than the promotion renewing, the Xero-versus-QuickBooks gap changes.
Whether Intuit publishes a price for Expert Full Service Bookkeeping. A visible number would make QuickBooks the clear pick for anyone wanting a human, and would let us rank it first.
MTD for Income Tax phasing in for UK sole traders. FreeAgent's free-with-NatWest tier plus HMRC filing gets much more valuable if it stays included, and much less if it is unbundled.
Bench under Employer.com. Two clean years of operation would make it re-listable; another wobble makes the point permanently.
Bank-feed reliability after open-banking consent rules change. Every ranking above assumes feeds keep working; 90-day reauthentication requirements have broken them before.

ops.screen-applicants.question: Which tool helps me screen a flood of applicants without handing me a bias audit bill and legal exposure?

method.how: Ranked on whether the tool gives you a defensible screening process, not on claimed accuracy — nobody publishes accuracy you can check. Three things drove the order: can you read a real price at source, does the tool score or rank applicants (which pulls you into NYC Local Law 144's bias-audit duty and the EU AI Act's high-risk tier), and does anyone publish an independent bias audit. Ashby is first because its AI deliberately refuses to rank or auto-reject, which keeps a human in the decision and the legal exposure smaller; Eightfold is here mainly because it is the only vendor in the set that publishes a dated, named, third-party audit. Nothing in this category screens well enough to trust unsupervised — every entry below is a filter, not a decision-maker.
method.tested_on: Not independently tested. No applicant pools were run through any of these tools. Prices, feature tiers and compliance claims were read from the vendors' own pages on 2026-08-29; the Local Law 144 and EU AI Act requirements were read from nyc.gov and the AI Act text.
method.conflicts: None. No affiliate links, no paid placements, no relationship with any tool listed.
method.blind_note: There is no independent benchmark for resume-screening quality — no shared test set, no published precision/recall for any of these products. Search results for 'best resume screening tool' are almost entirely vendors and affiliates ranking themselves. The only third-party evidence found was Eightfold's NYC Local Law 144 audit by BABL AI, and that measures demographic impact ratios, not whether the screening is any good.

ranked.name: Ashby
ranked.one_liner: AI that assists the review and refuses to rank candidates
ranked.use_it_when: You are a 20-100 person company drowning in inbound applications and you want structured criteria, citations and an audit trail rather than a black-box score.
ranked.cost: Foundations $400/month flat, up to 100 employees. Above that, quote only.
ranked.pricing_detail: Foundations: $400/month for companies up to 100 employees, flat rate, 10% discount for an annual commitment, 1,500 AI credits per month. Plus (101-1,000 employees) and Enterprise (1,000+) are custom-priced 'based on company size, usage, and commitment'. Ashby Analytics is a separate usage-priced product for 100+ employees.
ranked.good_at: Structured, explainable review. Ashby states its AI 'never 'ranks' or gives numerical ratings to applicants, a human must always be involved in decision-making', gives citations for every AI output, warns in-app when your criteria look discriminatory, and says it has run third-party bias audits with FairNow. Flat monthly pricing rather than per-seat is unusual and cheap once you have more than three recruiters.
ranked.the_catch: $400/month is a flat fee whether you hire two people or two hundred — a team making a handful of hires a year is paying roughly $2,400 per hire in tooling. Foundations includes 1,500 AI credits a month and the pricing page does not state what an extra credit costs, so heavy application volume has an unpriced ceiling. And 'never ranks' cuts both ways: it filters and surfaces, it does not clear your queue for you.
ranked.wrong_for: Anyone over 100 employees who needs a number before a sales call — you will be quoted. Solo recruiters and agencies billing per seat should look at Manatal instead; if you need a published bias audit to hand your legal team, Eightfold is the only one here that has one.

ranked.name: Workable
ranked.one_liner: Real 0-100 scores, real credit meter, real compliance homework
ranked.use_it_when: High inbound volume, small team, and you actually want the tool to triage — auto-advance the strong fits and route out the clear no's rather than just highlight them.
ranked.cost: From $299/month. AI agent is an add-on billed in credits.
ranked.pricing_detail: Standard $299/month or $3,588/year; Premier $599/month or $7,188/year; Enterprise $719/month or $8,628/year (vendor states 20% saving on annual). All plans include 3,000 free AI credits; Workable Agent is an add-on. Credit packs: 5,000 for $600 ($0.12/credit), 10,000 for $1,000 ($0.10), 50,000 for $4,750 ($0.095). Credits expire one year from purchase and are non-refundable.
ranked.good_at: Actual triage. Workable states the agent 'evaluates candidates against up to 14 criteria specific to your job. Each criterion is scored independently and then normalized to a 0-100 scale', shows the reasoning, moves strong candidates to a shortlist and messages candidates to fill gaps. Published, readable prices on every tier — rare in this category.
ranked.the_catch: Two traps. First, the credits: the base subscription includes 3,000 and after that you are buying packs that expire in twelve months and cannot be refunded, so a hiring freeze burns money you already spent. Second, and larger — a normalised 0-100 score that auto-advances candidates is the textbook automated employment decision tool. If you hire in New York City that triggers Local Law 144: an annual independent bias audit, a published summary with impact ratios, and 10 business days' notice to candidates before you use it. Workable's AI page says the agent 'is aligned with the EU AI Act' but publishes no Local Law 144 bias audit, so that audit is your bill, not theirs.
ranked.wrong_for: NYC employers who have no budget or appetite for an annual independent audit — use Ashby, whose AI does not score or auto-reject. Also wrong if you hire fewer than about ten people a year; $299/month plus credits is a lot of overhead for a trickle.

ranked.name: Eightfold AI
ranked.one_liner: The only one that publishes its bias audit in full
ranked.use_it_when: Enterprise hiring at volume in regulated or litigation-exposed environments, where legal will ask for the audit before procurement will sign.
ranked.cost: No price published anywhere. Quote only.
ranked.pricing_detail: Eightfold publishes no pricing tiers, no per-seat rate and no starting price. Expect an enterprise sales cycle and an annual contract.
ranked.good_at: Transparency about disparate impact. The Matching Model audit was conducted by BABL AI Inc., audit dated 3 March 2026 and signed 26 March 2026, covering 29 million candidate assessments from January 2024 to December 2025. Reported scoring rates: female 62.8% (reference), male 60.5%, impact ratio 0.962. By race/ethnicity, Hispanic or Latino 67.2% as reference, with impact ratios from 0.938 (Asian) to 0.986 (American Indian/Alaskan Native) — all above the 0.80 four-fifths threshold. The AI Interviewer is audited separately. Eightfold also cites ISO/IEC 42001:2023, SOC 2 Type II and FedRAMP.
ranked.the_catch: You cannot find out what it costs without talking to sales, and there is no self-serve entry point — this is a platform purchase, not a screening add-on. More important: the vendor's audit does not discharge your duty. Under Local Law 144 the liability sits with the employer or employment agency, which must have a bias audit no more than a year old covering the tool as it is actually used, publish the summary on its own site, and give candidates notice 10 business days before use. Eightfold's published audit is a strong starting point and evidence of good faith; it is not your compliance.
ranked.wrong_for: Anyone under a few hundred employees, or anyone who needs to start screening this week. Use Ashby or Workable. If you want the audit-quality signal without enterprise procurement, ask Ashby for its FairNow audit work in writing.

ranked.name: Manatal
ranked.one_liner: Cheapest real scoring engine, zero published bias evidence
ranked.use_it_when: Recruitment agency or lean in-house team outside NYC, screening on a budget, where $15 per seat matters more than an audit trail.
ranked.cost: From $15/user/month billed annually ($19 monthly).
ranked.pricing_detail: Professional $15/user/month annual, $19 monthly — up to 15 jobs and 10,000 candidates. Enterprise $35 annual, $39 monthly — unlimited jobs and candidates, workflow automation. Enterprise Plus $55 annual, $59 monthly — advanced report builder, API access, SSO, priority support. Custom plan on request. AI candidate recommendations and scoring are included on all three published tiers.
ranked.good_at: Price per seat and requirement-level explanation. Manatal states candidates are 'scored and ranked immediately based on your specific job criteria' and gives a requirement-by-requirement analysis showing where each candidate matched or failed. At $15 a seat it undercuts everything else here that scores at all.
ranked.the_catch: It scores and ranks every applicant on arrival and publishes no bias audit, no impact ratios and no EU AI Act documentation on its public pages — its own FAQ acknowledges 'the risk of perpetuating existing biases' without saying how it is tested. That combination is the worst case for a NYC employer: full AEDT exposure, no vendor evidence to lean on. Also per-seat, so a five-person team is $75/month, not $15, and API access and SSO are gated to the $55 tier — nearly four times the advertised entry price.
ranked.wrong_for: NYC employers and anyone selling into the EU who will need high-risk documentation from the provider — Eightfold or Ashby are the defensible choices. Skip it too if you want flat pricing rather than per-seat: Ashby is $400 flat regardless of headcount.

ranked.name: Odoo Recruitment
ranked.one_liner: Free, self-hostable pipeline that deliberately ranks nothing
ranked.use_it_when: Candidate data cannot leave your infrastructure, or your budget is zero and you would rather read CVs yourself than defend an algorithm.
ranked.cost: Free forever for one app, unlimited users. Self-host Community free. Paid from $24.90/user/month annual.
ranked.pricing_detail: Odoo Online 'One App Free': one app, unlimited users, hosting and support included. Standard $24.90/user/month yearly or $31.10 monthly (all apps). Custom $49.00/user/month yearly or $61.00 monthly — adds Studio, multi-company, external API and the option to deploy on Odoo.sh or on-premise. Community edition is downloadable and self-hostable under LGPLv3 (confirmed in the repository LICENSE file), which permits commercial use. Some AI and enrichment features are in-app purchases outside the subscription.
ranked.good_at: Costing nothing and creating no algorithmic liability. Unlimited users on the free tier is genuinely unusual. Screening is manual plus custom tests sent to candidates — 'thin the pool' by assessment, not by score — which is exactly what you want if you have no appetite for an audit. LGPLv3 self-hosting means candidate data never leaves your servers, which also sidesteps most of the transfer questions.
ranked.the_catch: It does not do the job the other four claim to do. There is no automated scoring or ranking of applicants, so at 500 applications a role you are still reading 500 CVs — the free price is paid in your time. The free tier is one app only: add anything else and every user jumps to $24.90/month yearly, and on-premise deployment of the paid version sits on the $49 Custom plan. Community edition is free but is the cut-down build, and self-hosting is your ops problem.
ranked.wrong_for: Anyone whose actual problem is volume — you need Workable or Manatal to triage. Use Odoo only if the constraint is data residency, budget, or a deliberate refusal to automate the decision.

also_considered.name: Greenhouse
also_considered.why_not: Best structured scorecards in the category, but Core, Plus and Pro are all quote-only — no number is readable at source, so we cannot rank it against priced tools.

also_considered.name: SmartRecruiters
also_considered.why_not: Essential is published as 'starting at $14,995' but AI-powered candidate screening only appears in the High Volume tier, which is quote-only.

also_considered.name: Zoho Recruit
also_considered.why_not: Genuinely free forever tier, but limited to 1 active job per recruiter licence and every paid price sits behind a calculator, so no figure could be read at source.

also_considered.name: HireVue
also_considered.why_not: Heavily used for screening, but its legal centre publishes no bias audit — third-party reports are only 'upon request', which is the opposite of what Local Law 144 asks you to post.

also_considered.name: OpenCATS
also_considered.why_not: Free, self-hosted, community-maintained (v0.10.0), but its own site describes no resume ranking or automated screening at all — it is a tracker, not a screener.

also_considered.name: Harver (with pymetrics and Outmatch)
also_considered.why_not: Assessment-led screening rather than resume screening; Outmatch has been folded into Harver and no pricing is published anywhere on the site.

watch_list: The EU AI Act deadline: Article 113 now applies Annex III high-risk obligations from 2 December 2027, not August 2026. Annex III point 4(a) explicitly covers systems used 'to analyse and filter job applications, and to evaluate candidates'. If that date moves again, the urgency of vendor documentation moves with it.

Whether Ashby, Workable, Greenhouse or Manatal start publishing dated, named, third-party bias audits the way Eightfold publishes BABL AI's. Today that is a one-vendor differentiator and it would reorder this list fast.
Ashby's AI credit overage rate. Foundations includes 1,500 credits a month and no overage price is published; if it is punitive, the flat $400 stops being flat.

Whether Workable folds agent screening into the base subscription. At $0.095-$0.12 a credit with twelve-month expiry, credits are the real cost; remove them and Workable's effective price undercuts Ashby.
Any other US state or city copying Local Law 144's annual-audit-plus-published-summary model. NYC is currently the sharp edge; a second jurisdiction changes the maths for every scoring tool here.
Whether any vendor starts indemnifying customers for AEDT compliance rather than leaving the employer to carry it.
